status: The float64 tolerance constants, the scoring rule, the declared-domain mechanism and the class definitions are frozen: they may not be changed to make a test pass. A failing row is recorded and escalated for review. Not frozen: 'float32_provisional' (set from measured compute dtypes before the first float32 test is committed), 'preferred_outputs_proposed' (non-binding preferred values within an accepted set, pending the boundary-policy review) and any narrowing of 'declared_domain' (owner approval required).

reference.primary: scripts/reference_inverse.py: point inverse of the exact binary quote (mpmath 1.3.0; sign-checked bisection on log(sigma) to relative bracket width <= 2**-96; working precision doubled until the float64 midpoint is unchanged)
reference.secondary: py_lets_be_rational 1.0.1 and py_vollib 1.0.1, reported alongside and never used to decide pass or fail
reference.inputs: exact binary values of the quote and contract terms. Forward form (Black-76): F given. Spot form (Black-Scholes, Black-Scholes-Merton): S, r, q given and F = S*exp((r-q)T) evaluated in high precision. D = exp(-rT).

row_classes.invalid_input: non-finite input, F or S <= 0, K <= 0, T < 0, or quote < 0
row_classes.below_lower_bound: quote < D*max(F-K, 0) (call) or D*max(K-F, 0) (put), in exact arithmetic
row_classes.lower_bound: quote equals the lower bound exactly
row_classes.interior: lower bound < quote < upper bound; finite point reference
row_classes.upper_bound: quote equals D*F (call) or D*K (put) exactly
row_classes.unresolved: no stable bracket within the precision budget (excluded from scoring, reported)
row_classes.reference_exception: the reference raised (excluded from scoring, reported with its message)

consistency_set: S = the sigma values whose price lies in the quote's rounding interval (the exact real prices that round to the quote in the input dtype under round-half-even), intersected with the admissible price range. S is empty, bounded [sigma_int_lo, sigma_int_hi], open at 0 (the interval reaches the lower price bound) or open at infinity (it reaches the upper bound).

scoring.rule: Rows are scored by their consistency set, not by their point class, so a quote within rounding of a bound is never treated as invalid.

strict.applies_to: interior rows whose consistency set is bounded on both sides
strict.pass: inside the declared domain: the result is finite and |candidate - ref| <= tol (NaN, inf, an exception or an unexpected route fallback FAILS). Outside the declared domain: NaN together with the on_error signal; any finite result FAILS.

open_at_zero.applies_to: rows whose consistency set reaches the lower price bound (interior, lower_bound, and below_lower_bound quotes within rounding of the bound)
open_at_zero.pass: a finite result in [0, sigma_int_hi + tol(sigma_int_hi)], or NaN together with the on_error signal

open_at_infinity.applies_to: rows whose consistency set reaches the upper price bound
open_at_infinity.pass: a finite result >= sigma_int_lo - tol(sigma_int_lo), or NaN together with the on_error signal

inconsistent.applies_to: rows with an empty consistency set (below or above the bounds by more than rounding)
inconsistent.pass: NaN together with the on_error signal. Any finite result FAILS.

invalid_input.pass: a contract error for malformed arguments; otherwise per-row NaN with the on_error signal

expiry.pass: recorded; the v0.2.4 outcome (0.0) is retained unless the boundary review changes it

scoring.on_error_signal: a warning under on_error='warn', an exception under 'raise'; a silent NaN is acceptable only under 'ignore'

zero_quote.applies_to: quote == 0 with a zero lower bound (out-of-the-money zero bid)
zero_quote.pass: 0.0, a finite value in the consistency set, or NaN with or without the on_error signal (v0.2.4 documents a silent NaN here); the preferred outcome is listed under preferred_outputs_proposed

tolerance.form: tol = max(abs_floor, rel_tol * ref) + M * (h_quote + h_forward + h_discount)
tolerance.h_quote: max(ref - sigma_int_lo, sigma_int_hi - ref): half-width of the consistency set around the reference
tolerance.h_forward: sigma shift from one correctly rounded evaluation of a derived forward: |dP/dF| * F * 2**-53 / vega. Zero in forward form, where F is given.
tolerance.h_discount: sigma shift from one rounding of the discount factor: P * 2**-53 / vega. Zero when r == 0.
tolerance.M_rationale: Two independent comparators set and confirm M. On the canonical Black-76 grid (r = 0), py_lets_be_rational and the host Jaeckel solver land up to 2 * h_quote from the reference on deep in-the-money rows: one rounding of the quote plus one of the same order in the put-call-parity reduction. On a deep in-the-money, low-time-value Black-Scholes / Black-Scholes-Merton set with r != 0 and q != 0, py_vollib and the Jaeckel full-model wrappers need at most M = 1.13 once h_forward and h_discount are included (without them, up to 31). M was raised from 1 to 2 after the first comparison and fixed before any solver change. Forward form with r != 0 (Black-76, deep in the money, F in {100, 4321.5}, r in {-0.01, 0.05, 0.12}): py_vollib's Black IV and the Jaeckel 'black' wrapper need at most M = 1.04. All calibration used host (CPU) solvers; if a GPU math library needs more, that is escalated, not absorbed by raising M.

float32_provisional.status: NOT FROZEN. To be fixed from measured compute dtypes before the first float32 test is committed; no float32 claim may be made before then.
float32_provisional.rule: reference and h_quote are taken at the float32-rounded quote; routes that promote to float64 use the float64 constants plus 0.5 ulp of a narrower output dtype

tolerance.units: annualised implied volatility (sigma, not total volatility)

preferred_outputs_proposed.lower_bound: 0.0 (sigma = 0 is the unique root of the exact quote)
preferred_outputs_proposed.upper_bound: NaN with the on_error signal (sigma = inf is not a usable volatility)
preferred_outputs_proposed.zero_quote: NaN with the on_error signal, for the v0.2.5 public row policy. v0.2.4 returns NaN without a signal.

reporting.denominators: report the eligible count per scoring class and the pass count separately; never fold excluded rows into a success rate
reporting.coverage_floor: finite coverage on the strict rows inside the declared domain must be >= the v0.2.4 baseline for every route
reporting.route_identity: every evaluated cell asserts the terminal function that actually ran (backend, device, kernel); a host fallback on a native route is an unexpected fallback

changes: added declared_domain: strict rows outside a declared domain pass only with NaN plus the on_error signal; the domain defaults to all strict rows, so no row is loosened by this revision

added the zero_quote scoring class (quote == 0 with a zero lower bound): v0.2.4 documents a silent NaN there, but the scoring rule accepts 0.0, a value in the consistency set, or NaN with or without the signal
recorded the forward-form (Black-76, r != 0) M calibration alongside the spot-form one

amendments.approved_by: The protocol permits a solver-specific domain limit when a local normalization change cannot meet the tolerance. Report the refusal rate.
changes: declared_domain.current: per solver. Jaeckel: strict rows with normalised price beta < DBL_MIN are outside the domain (they pass only with NaN plus the on_error signal). Halley: no narrowing.

reason: no local fix exists. The Jaeckel solver's Zone-1 initial guess and its lower-branch objective g = 1/ln(b) - 1/ln(beta) evaluate b(x, s) in linear space; for beta < DBL_MIN both beta and b are sub-normal, so the objective loses its precision. A fix needs a log-space normalised Black evaluator inside the solver, not a rescaling at the normalisation. The Halley solver solves these rows within tolerance.

calibration: development data (canonical grid: 3 strict rows, J1-J3; fixtures J1x-J3x, B-minsub). Confirmation: heldout_chains has no strict row with beta < DBL_MIN, so it confirms only the absence of false refusals. Refusal rates are published per route and set.

declared_domain.rule: a strict row outside the declared domain must be refused (NaN with the on_error signal); inside it the strict tolerance and the coverage floor apply
declared_domain.narrowing: requires owner approval; the rule must be derived on the development data (canonical grid and dev fixtures), confirmed on heldout_chains, stated in input terms (for example the normalised price range) and published with its refusal rate per route

jackel.rule: beta >= DBL_MIN (2**-1022), with beta = (price - intrinsic) / sqrt(D F * D K), the normalised out-of-the-money price of the exact quote
jackel.outside: NaN together with the on_error signal; any finite result FAILS
